criteria.criterion: The job report states the cause of the flake and the evidence for it: reproduction output under load, plus the code lines involved in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs.
criteria.evidence: Athena's producer-report-gaps record says the producer's report still did not cover this criterion after its send-back. The evidence snapshot under records/jobs/2026-11/20261106-080857-9daz/ holds only request.json, reading-1.json, priority-1.json and the reader invocation, with no producer report or reproduction output. The cause is written only in the CHANGELOG and a test comment, and it matches the code I read: drain.rs:3703 writes the stop file, :3704 calls drain_state, and linux_marker at :3426 returns None for a zombie (Z/X). No output from a run under load is shown that proves this is the failure seen on 6 Nov.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file_when_command_lines_contain_drain` 200 times in a row while other cargo tests run in parallel. Every run passes, and the recorded check output shows the loop.
criteria.evidence: The only recorded checks are the CI fmt, clippy and test runs, which are single runs. No recorded check output shows a 200-run loop under load. I ran the test once in the snapshot and it passed (1 passed, finished in 0.02s). That is one run on an idle machine, not 200 runs under load. A shell loop is not among the commands I am allowed to run.

criteria.criterion: In the diff, the test still writes a pid file naming only the real drain child. It still starts a decoy with arg0 'athena drain --budget 9' that is not in the pid file. It still asserts that drain_state returns Running(record), that the status text has the drain pid and not the decoy pid, that the stop outcomes are Asked and then Exited, and that the decoy is still alive at the end.
criteria.evidence: Read drain.rs:5051-5114. write_record(root, &record_of(drain_child.id(), BUILD)) is unchanged, and so is sleeper("athena drain --budget 9"). The assertions are all unchanged: Running(found)==record, the status contains the drain pid and not the decoy pid, Asked(record.clone()), Exited(record), settled is Dead, and decoy try_wait is None. The diff adds only a second argument for the release file to the script, the condition `|| [ ! -e "$2" ]`, and a std::fs::write(&release) after the Asked checks.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry that describes only what the diff does, with no claims beyond it.
criteria.evidence: The new entry under ### Fixed describes the release-file change, says only that test changed and that no production code changed, and says the pid-file and decoy checks are as before. All of these match the diff. The opening line "no longer fails at random on a busy machine" states the intended effect, which has not been measured (see the minor finding).

findings.summary: The cause was never confirmed by a reproduction under load
findings.evidence: The request asks for the cause to be found "from a reproduction under load" and stated with evidence. Athena's producer-report-gaps record says this was not reported, and the evidence snapshot has no producer report. The stated cause fits the code (drain.rs:3703-3704, 3426), but nothing shows that this race produced the failures on 6 Nov rather than some other timing issue. The root-cause default requires the cause to be reproduced and stated.

Criterion 2 needs recorded check output that shows the loop. The only records are single CI runs of fmt, clippy and test. My single targeted run passed, but that shows nothing about determinism under load.

findings.evidence: "no longer fails at random on a busy machine" is the expected effect, but no loop run backs it. Once the loop has been recorded, the line stands.

summary: The candidate fails: the fix looks correct, but there is no proof that the flake's cause was found or that it is gone. The code change is small and sound. The test's stand-in drain used to exit as soon as the stop file appeared, and `stop_and_wait` writes that file (drain.rs:3703) before it checks the drain (:3704). A stand-in that exits in that gap becomes a zombie, and `linux_marker` (:3426) reads a zombie as dead. Now the stand-in also waits for a release file that the test creates only after the ask-only checks. The pid-file and decoy assertions are unchanged in meaning, only the two expected files changed, and fmt, clippy and the tests passed in Athena's recorded CI run. I ran the test once in the snapshot and it passed. Two of the request's acceptance criteria have no evidence. No job report states the cause with reproduction output from a run under load. No recorded check output shows the test passing 200 runs in a row under load. I could not run that loop myself, because a shell loop is not among the commands I may run. To pass, the producer needs to record a reproduction under load (ideally failing on the base commit), the 200-run loop passing on the candidate, and a report that states the cause with that output.
